summary: Sixty days of PET or low density polyethylene microplastics lowered red cells and haemoglobin and damaged liver, kidney, intestine and gills in walking catfish.
Combined polypropylene microplastics and the plasticiser DEHP caused neuronal apoptosis and neuroinflammation in immature mice.
Review and field investigation estimating that haemodialysis patients face high risk of micro and nanoplastic contamination from dialysis water.
Sixty days of polyethylene microplastics in soil impaired earthworm growth, reproduction, detoxification capacity and energy metabolism.
Review of pharmaceuticals, microplastics and co-infecting microbes after COVID-19 and implications for antimicrobial resistance; an environmental policy review.
Polystyrene nanoplastics lowered the nutritional quality of jacopever more than microplastics by disturbing mitochondrial electron transfer and liver metabolism.
Polystyrene nanoplastics drove testicular inflammation by promoting M1 macrophage infiltration and a reactive oxygen species burst with energy metabolism disorder.
Review of 91 human biomonitoring studies on microplastics in human matrices and the health implications they suggest.
Microplastics found in Indian bottled water, mostly polyethylene, downregulated antioxidant defence genes in zebrafish embryos concentration and time dependently.
Review drawing parallels between particle-induced lung overload and polyethylene wear particle-induced periprosthetic osteolysis as adverse outcome pathways.
Six to nine weeks of dietary polyethylene microbeads caused inflammatory and metabolic change in mouse liver and worsened chemically induced fibrosis.
Ciprofloxacin adsorbed to aged polystyrene fragments and desorbed differently in simulated gastric and intestinal fluids, supporting a carrier role.
Speculative review of how climate change may alter oesophageal disease patterns; no plastic particle exposure.
Polystyrene nanoplastics aggravated dibutyl phthalate-induced blood-testis barrier dysfunction in mice by suppressing autophagy, which reactivation relieved.
Critical review building an adverse outcome pathway for microplastic toxicity in the human gastrointestinal tract after oral exposure.
Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene microplastics raised earthworm bioaccumulation of a brominated flame retardant by adsorption and their own toxicity.
Low-dose polystyrene microplastics induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and in human-derived cardiac organoids, raising hypertrophic gene expression.
Short-term polyethylene microplastic exposure changed earthworm metabolome and gut microbiota without visible growth or mortality effects.
Narrative review of airborne microplastic characteristics, respiratory tract deposition, translocation and the toxic effects reported in vitro and in vivo.
Nanoplastics suppressed Wnt signalling genes in human brain organoids, suggesting adverse effects on embryonic brain development.
Five sizes of polystyrene nanoplastics produced size-dependent cytotoxic and immunotoxic effects on mouse and human liver cells and on mouse liver and gut.
Tetracycline and ciprofloxacin adsorbed to polypropylene microfibres were highly bioaccessible in simulated human gastric and intestinal fluids.
Polystyrene nanoplastics activated innate immunity and disturbed metabolism in human lung cells through the cGAS and STING pathway, eased by prostaglandin B1.
State of science review of micro and nanoplastic toxicological outcomes, setting out knowledge gaps and the need for environmentally relevant exposures.
Polystyrene nanoplastics with a polychlorinated biphenyl caused oxidative stress, histopathology and intestinal microbiota disruption in a hard clam.
